STEP 1 - Scene: This looks like a small portion of mashed or puréed potato (or possibly mashed cauliflower, given the pale green-tinged piece) on a white square plate. Photographed from above, nearly straight down, so the plate outline is close to true proportion.

STEP 2 - Ruler: White square plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 26 × 26 × 0.85 (rounded corners) ≈ 575 cm², so I use ~550 cm² of usable plate area.

STEP 3 - Items: (1) mashed/puréed pale yellow starchy food (potato-like), in several lumps on the right side; (2) a small pale green piece at the centre-right, likely cauliflower or a bit of vegetable mixed into the mash.

STEP 4 - Area: Mashed food together covers about 12% of the plate (~66 cm²). The pale green piece is about 2% (~11 cm²). Total food coverage ≈ 14%, consistent with the scattered pile on the right.

STEP 5 - Volume: Mashed mound: 66 cm² × 2 cm average height ≈ 130 ml. Green piece: 11 cm² × 1.5 cm ≈ 16 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams: Mashed food at 0.9 g/ml: 130 × 0.9 ≈ 117 g. Green vegetable piece at 0.6 g/ml: 16 × 0.6 ≈ 10 g.

STEP 7 - Energy: Mashed potato ≈ 90 kcal/100 g (cooked, as plated, with some butter/milk): 117 × 0.9 ≈ 105 kcal. Cooked cauliflower/green vegetable ≈ 25 kcal/100 g: 10 × 0.25 ≈ 3 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: The visible amount is a modest side-dish portion, far less than a full plate. About 127 g total and ~108 kcal is plausible for what is shown, given the plate is only partly covered.
